items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: working with Bobby Doland on certain TV scores

ctx.x: Why it took the shape it did I can't ascribe to anything else except I wanted to do something for strings. I lost my fear of it because they would never let me handle these things. I wasn't a string man. They used to label you; they still do. If you're a jazz man you can't be something else. You know how it is.

I lost my fear of it through working on shows and working with Bobby Doland on certain TV scores. Then it gave me a chance--how to make it work for Stan was a big problem and it took me a long time to figure that one out, because I didn't
want to write goose eggs. I didn't want to write the smathered rhythm section because to me that wouldn't have been any fun. There's nothing wrong with it, but I didn't want to do that.
